```{r}
library(haven)
library(dplyr)

#load w1 to w4
w1 <- load("data w1 to w4/21600-0001-Data copy.rda") # Wave I in-home
w2<- load("data w1 to w4/21600-0005-Data copy.rda") # Wave II in-home
w3 <- load("data w1 to w4/21600-0008-Data copy.rda") # Wave III in-home
w4 <- load("data w1 to w4/21600-0022-Data copy.rda") # Wave IV in-home

View(w4)

#Each wave file has hundreds of variables. If you merge everything first, you end up with a dataset thousands of columns wide, which is slow and confusing. Instead, select your variables of interest from each wave first, keeping AID in every one:
w1_sub <- w1 %>% select(AID, 
                         GSWGT1,      # Wave I cross-sectional weight
                         CLUSTER2,    # PSU variable (needed for all analyses)
                         REGION,      # stratification variable
                         # --- your W1 variables here ---
                         # --- Race -----
                         H1GI6A,      # race (Hispanic)
                         H1GI6B,      # race (White)
                         H1GI6B,      # race (Black or African American)
                         H1GI6C,      # race (American Indian or Native American)
                         H1GI6D,      # race (Asian or Pacific Islander)
                         H1GI6E,      # race (Other)
                         # --- AGE ----
                         H1GI9,       # age at Wave I
                         PA12,        # parental education (from parent questionnaire)
                         PA55,       # family income
                        # ---- SEX ----
                        BIO_SEX,     #male/female/refused
   #------ Section 10: Feelings Scale (Depression) ------
                        H1FS1,        # You were bothered by things that usually don’t bother you.
                        H1FS2,        # You didn’t feel like eating, your appetite was poor.
                        H1FS3,        # You felt that you could not shake off the blues, even with help from your                                          family and your friends.
                        H1FS4,        # You felt that you were just as good as other people.
                        H1FS5,        # You had trouble keeping your mind on what you were doing.
                        H1FS6,        # You felt depressed.
                        H1FS7,        # You felt that you were too tired to do things.
                        H1FS8,        # You felt hopeful about the future.
                        H1FS9,        # You thought your life had been a failure.
                        H1FS10,       # You felt fearful.
                        H1FS11,       # You were happy
                        H1FS12,       # You talked less than usual.
                        H1FS13,       # You felt lonely.
                        H1FS14,       # People were unfriendly to you
                        H1FS15,       # You enjoyed life.
                        H1FS16,       # You felt sad.
                        H1FS17,       # You felt that people disliked you.
                        H1FS18,       # It was hard to get started doing things.
                        H1FS19,      # You felt life was not worth living
                        #---------Parent Relationships-----------
  # ---- Section 16: Relations with Parents (autonomy / decision-making) ----
  H1WP1,    # Q1  Parents let you decide your own weekend-night curfew?
  H1WP2,    # Q2  Parents let you decide the people you hang around with?
  H1WP3,    # Q3  Parents let you decide what you wear?
  H1WP4,    # Q4  Parents let you decide how much TV you watch?
  H1WP5,    # Q5  Parents let you decide which TV programs you watch?
  H1WP6,    # Q6  Parents let you decide what time you go to bed on week nights?
  H1WP7,    # Q7  Parents let you decide what you eat?
  H1WP8,    # Q8  # of past 7 days a parent was in the room while you ate evening meal

  # ---- Section 16: closeness / caring / educational aspirations (MOTHER) ----
  H1WP9,    # Q9   How close do you feel to your mother?
  H1WP10,   # Q10  How much do you think she cares about you?
  H1WP11,   # Q11  How disappointed would she be if you did NOT graduate college? (1-5)
  H1WP12,   # Q12  How disappointed would she be if you did NOT graduate high school? (1-5)

  # ---- Section 16: closeness / caring / educational aspirations (FATHER) ----
  H1WP13,   # Q13  How close do you feel to your father?
  H1WP14,   # Q14  How much do you think he cares about you?
  H1WP15,   # Q15  How disappointed would he be if you did NOT graduate college? (1-5)
  H1WP16,   # Q16  How disappointed would he be if you did NOT graduate high school? (1-5)

  # ---- Section 16 Q17: activities done with MOTHER in past 4 weeks ----
  H1WP17A,  # Q17a  gone shopping
  H1WP17B,  # Q17b  played a sport
  H1WP17C,  # Q17c  gone to a religious service / church event
  H1WP17D,  # Q17d  talked about someone you're dating or a party you went to
  H1WP17E,  # Q17e  gone to a movie, play, museum, concert, or sports event
  H1WP17F,  # Q17f  had a talk about a personal problem you were having
  H1WP17G,  # Q17g  had a serious argument about your behavior
  H1WP17H,  # Q17h  talked about your school work or grades
  H1WP17I,  # Q17i  worked on a project for school
  H1WP17J,  # Q17j  talked about other things you're doing in school
  H1WP17K,  # Q17k  none of the above

  # ---- Section 16 Q18: activities done with FATHER in past 4 weeks ----
  H1WP18A,  # Q18a  gone shopping
  H1WP18B,  # Q18b  played a sport
  H1WP18C,  # Q18c  gone to a religious service / church event
  H1WP18D,  # Q18d  talked about someone you're dating or a party you went to
  H1WP18E,  # Q18e  gone to a movie, play, museum, concert, or sports event
  H1WP18F,  # Q18f  had a talk about a personal problem you were having
  H1WP18G,  # Q18g  had a serious argument about your behavior
  H1WP18H,  # Q18h  talked about your school work or grades
  H1WP18I,  # Q18i  worked on a project for school
  H1WP18J,  # Q18j  talked about other things you're doing in school
  H1WP18K,  # Q18k  none of the above

  # ---- Section 18****: warmth / communication / satisfaction (MOTHER) ----
  H1PF1,    # Q1   Most of the time, your mother is warm and loving toward you
  H1PF2,    # Q2   Your mother encourages you to be independent
  H1PF3,    # Q3   When you do wrong, your mother talks it through & helps you understand why
  H1PF4,    # Q4   You are satisfied with the way your mother and you communicate
  H1PF5,    # Q5   Overall, you are satisfied with your relationship with your mother

  # ---- Section 18: warmth / communication / satisfaction (FATHER) ----
  H1PF23,   # Q23  Most of the time, your father is warm and loving toward you
  H1PF24,   # Q24  You are satisfied with the way your father and you communicate
  H1PF25    # Q25  Overall, you are satisfied with your relationship with your father
)
```
